'''Aristides Baltas''' ({{langx|el|Αριστείδης Μπαλτάς}}; born 9 February 1943) is a [[philosophy of science|philosopher of science]] and [[physicist]] who served as the [[Ministry of Culture and Sports (Greece)|Minister of Culture and Sports]] of [[Greece]] and as the [[Ministry of Culture, Education and Religious Affairs|Minister of Culture, Education and Religious Affairs]] in the [[First Cabinet of Alexis Tsipras|cabinet of Alexis Tsipras]] from 27 January 2015 to 4 November 2016.

He is currently the Emeritus Professor of Philosophy of Science at the [[National Technical University of Athens]] and President of the [[Nicos Poulantzas]] Institute.<ref name="To Vima">{{cite news|url=http://www.tovima.gr/society/article/?aid=670837|title="Διαφωνούμε κάθετα με το νόμο πλαίσιο" λέει ο Αριστείδης Μπαλτάς|newspaper=[[To Vima]]|date=26 January 2015|access-date=29 January 2015}}</ref> In the [[September 2015 Greek legislative election]], he was elected [[Hellenic Parliament|MP]] for the [[Attica constituency]] with [[SYRIZA]].

==Education and academic career==

Baltas trained in electrical and mechanical engineering at the [[National Technical University of Athens]] (NTUA) from 1962 to 1967 before going on to complete a doctorate in theoretical physics under {{Interlanguage link multi|François Lurçat|fr}} at [[University of Paris XI]] in 1971. His thesis title was ''La Neutrino-Production des Résonances Baryoniques dans le Modèle des Quarks'' ("Neutrino Production of Baryonic Resonances in the Quark Model").<ref>{{cite web|url=http://didefth.gr/new/wp-content/uploads/Mpaltas_cv.pdf|title=Aristides Baltas – CV|accessdate=8 April 2016|archive-date=19 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419005749/http://didefth.gr/new/wp-content/uploads/Mpaltas_cv.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1982, he returned to NTUA to become a lecturer at the Department of Physics.<ref name="To Vima" /> From 1984 to 1985 he was a visiting fellow at the Center for Philosophy of Science of the [[University of Pittsburgh]], a capacity he later resumed in 2005–6.<ref name="Pittsburgh">{{cite web|url=http://www.pitt.edu/~pittcntr/People/visiting_fellows/VF_2005-06/baltas.htm|title=Center for Philosophy of Science: Visiting Fellows 2005–6|publisher=University of Pittsburgh|access-date=29 January 2015}}</ref> He was appointed assistant professor of philosophy and methodology of physics at NTUA in 1984, then associate professor of the philosophy of science in 1992 and professor in 2002.<ref name="To Vima" />

Baltas's research has dealt particularly with the [[epistemology]] of [[Louis Althusser]], and more generally with the relationship between philosophy of science and epistemology and between [[analytic philosophy|analytic]] and [[continental philosophy]].<ref name="To Vima" /><ref name="Pittsburgh" /> His work encompasses the fields of physics, [[mathematics]], [[psychoanalysis]], and [[historical materialism]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hellenic.as.nyu.edu/object/hellenics.aristides.baltas|title=Between Spinoza and Wittgenstein: A Panel Discussion on Aristides Baltas' Peeling Potatoes or Grinding Lenses.|publisher=New York University|access-date=30 January 2015}}</ref> Other philosophers studied by Baltas include [[Ludwig Wittgenstein]], [[Friedrich Nietzsche]], [[Baruch Spinoza]], [[Jacques Derrida]], [[John McDowell]], and [[Walter Benjamin]].<ref name="To Vima" />

===Awards===

In 2002, Baltas was awarded the National Prize for Nonfiction for his book ''Objects and Aspects of Self'' (Αντικείμενα και όψεις εαυτού).<ref>{{cite book|title=Freud and Fundamentalism: The Psychical Politics of Knowledge|editor=Stathis Gourgouris|page=247|year=2010|publisher=Fordham University Press|isbn=9780823232239|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HRZ-0xTbR_sC&pg=PA247}}</ref> In December 2010, he received the Xanthopoulos–Pneumatikos Award for Excellence in Academic Teaching.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ite.gr/index_main.php?l=e&c=54&i=1|title=Awards|publisher=[[Foundation for Research & Technology – Hellas]]|access-date=30 January 2015}}</ref>

==Political career==

A founding member of the [[Coalition of the Radical Left]] (SYRIZA), in 2012 Baltas was a coordinating member of its policy planning committee.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://socialistregister.com/index.php/srv/article/view/18813|title=The rise of Syriza: an interview with Aristides Baltas|journal=[[Socialist Register]]|volume=49|year=2013|author1=Aristides Baltas|author2=Leo Panitch}}</ref> Following the victory of SYRIZA in the [[January 2015 Greek legislative election|Greek legislative election of January 2015]], Baltas was appointed  [[Ministry of Culture, Education and Religious Affairs|Minister of Culture, Education and Religious Affairs]] in the [[First Cabinet of Alexis Tsipras|Tsipras Cabinet]]. Soon after entering office, Baltas stated that beyond the immediate objectives of relieving the humanitarian crisis in Greek schools and resolving the problem of "eternal students" who are forced to suspend their studies in order to find work to sustain themselves, his long-term goals as minister would be to restore the independence of secondary education from higher education, to abolish [[Apolytirion|pan-Hellenic examinations]], and to support [[free education|free access to higher education]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.universityworldnews.com/article.php?story=20150205101628484|title=Minister prepares to address 'human crisis'|author=Makki Marseilles|date=6 February 2015|access-date=8 February 2015|newspaper=[[University World News]]}}</ref>
